digest.component_or_area: tickets branch history reclamation / git-backed store compaction
propositions: The blobless CI checkout pack on tickets branch exceeds 481 MiB versus a 100 MiB budget; retired-event GC alone shrinks it by ~0 because .retired files are blobs and the guarded pack is blobless.

Safe reclamation requires a causal-stability boundary (C1-C5): folded event, remote-aged SNAPSHOT (≥N days reachable on sync remote), stale-clone forced override (>N days forced to reset), signature carriage in authorship_ledger or enforce_since re-anchor, and no unfolded state dependence.

The real pack-shrink lever is below-horizon commit/tree collapse into SNAPSHOT checkpoints via core-git fast-import rewrite, not .retired tombstone removal; this requires per-backend publish-swap (git-ref CAS for bare/GitHub/Gerrit; S3 exclusive bundle-set replacement bypassing auto-doctor) and ledger position→commit_sha re-resolution plus enforce_since re-anchor.

Maximal safe history coalescing at N=30d achieves ~365-380 MiB (insufficient); sub-4-day horizon would reach ≤100 MiB but is unsafe; a temporary budget-raise bridge (W3) plus structural fixes (W1 batch enrichment writes, W2 shard root-tree dirs) are unavoidable.

No destructive history rewrite, force-push, or bundle replacement may execute without human approval; the mechanism must be proven on a disposable shadow clone with rebar verify-authorship clean and pack shrinkage measured before any production swap.

Operator-approved remote-anchored horizon model (option 2) plus stale-clone forced override accepts residual >N-day loss; acceptance requires S0 ADR amending concurrency.md §I1 doctrine and proving I1-I9 under the horizon with override.
